notes.nzuukuka: Ninsisimuka, I wake up; Ninyimuka, I get up.
notes.nneebaka: Nimbyama, I sleep / I’m going to bed.

guidebook.intro: Talk about your day from waking up to going to sleep. The verb’s first letters say who is doing it.

tips.title: Who is doing it
body: The present starts with **ni-** and then the person: **ninkora** (I work), **nookora** (you work), **naakora** (he or she works), **nitukora** (we work), **nimukora** (you all work), **nibakora** (they work).

tips.title: Ku-: the verb’s name
body: The dictionary form of a verb starts with **ku-** (or **oku-**): **kusoma** (to read), **kuzaana** (to play). Use it after verbs like “like”: **Ninkunda kusoma** (I like reading).

culture.title: Early mornings
body: Village days start before sunrise with milking the cows. Children often fetch water and help with chores before walking to school.
